# DeepSeek Harness (dsh) version pin (phase 17A-06, Directive 4a / D-08)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# The agent console embedded by the Agent tab. Adopted rather than built,
# per 17A-06-DECISIONS.md: itembank does not maintain an agent console.
#
# PINNED VERSION
#   @deepseek-ai/dsh  0.1.0-rc.7
#   license:   MIT (package.json of the installed build, and the npm registry
#              `license` field, both read 2026-08-21)
#   tarball:   https://registry.npmjs.org/@deepseek-ai/dsh/-/dsh-0.1.0-rc.7.tgz
#   shasum:    8a69013c06179d7af437de92fb4a9a2e1fd7d410
#   integrity: sha512-ZceDCJ8FAywih+USW/OMk9jEhunlvJBGEz4kqrhau23hPzbciOaz
#              ZrywH0nBRsaalSeAJ1JGBmjtw4OSjToStw==
#   node:      verified on v22.22.3 (the version recorded in 13-RESEARCH.md
#              section 5 for the Tauri CLI, so this adds no new runtime)
#
# This is the exact build that was installed and run on 2026-08-21, not the
# newest one. The registry already carries 0.1.1-rc.2. An upgrade is a
# deliberate, tested change, for the reason recorded in 17A-06-DECISIONS.md:
# the README documents a `--no-open` flag that the published build rejects,
# and AGENTS.md states SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION 0 with no compatibility
# promise. The developer preview showed its teeth on the first day of
# contact.
#
# WHY THE TOP-LEVEL VERSION IS NOT THE PIN
#   Measured 2026-08-21: the package declares roughly sixty first-party
#   dependencies (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`) and every one of them is a CARET
#   range, `^0.1.0-rc.7`. For a 0.x version a caret still admits everything
#   below 0.2.0, so `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.7` resolves a
#   DIFFERENT tree tomorrow than it did today. Pinning the top-level version
#   alone pins almost nothing.
#
#   How far that drifts, measured 2026-08-21: a lockfile generated from the
#   top-level pin alone resolved 185 of the 191 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages
#   to 0.1.0-rc.8, while the install that was verified running has rc.7
#   throughout. Same top-level version, a different program. The overrides in
#   deps/dsh/package.json therefore hold the whole scope at rc.7, so the
#   locked tree is the tree that was tested rather than merely a tree that
#   resolves.
#
#   The real pin is therefore the lockfile beside this note:
#
#       deps/dsh/package.json        the exact top-level version
#       deps/dsh/package-lock.json   the resolved tree, with an integrity
#                                    hash for every transitive package
#
#   Reproduce that tree with:
#
#       cd deps/dsh && npm ci
#
#   `deps/dsh/` is a pin, not a build input. Nothing in itembank imports from
#   it and no shipped command reads it. It exists so the console the Agent tab
#   frames can be reinstalled byte-for-byte.
#
#   The two overrides are load-bearing and are not preferences:
#     @aws-sdk/core 3.977.8   a transitive package demands ^3.977.9, which the
#                             registry does not carry (highest 3.977.8,
#                             checked 2026-08-21). Without this the install
#                             fails outright with ETARGET.
#     @deepseek-ai/dsh-* rc.7 holds the scope at the tested version rather than
#                             letting the carets walk it forward to rc.8.
#   Remove either one and `npm ci` stops reproducing what was verified.
#
# EGRESS
#   Whatever provider the learner's own `dsh` config names. Verified running
#   on this machine 2026-08-21 against `qwen3.8-27b:latest` under the
#   `weibao-planing` profile, which keeps traffic on the machine. `dsh` reads
#   its own configuration and itembank does not set it, so the Agent tab
#   cannot promise where a `dsh` session's text goes. It says so rather than
#   claiming local.
#
# FRAMING
#   Verified 2026-08-21 by running `dsh web --port 3080`: no
#   X-Frame-Options, no Content-Security-Policy, no frame-ancestors. It
#   frames. The served document is `<html lang="zh-CN">`, so the embedding
#   page sets the locale explicitly rather than inheriting it.
#
# THE PYTHON SDK IS NOT PINNED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT PUBLISHED
#   17A-06-DECISIONS.md names `deepseek-harness-sdk` as the package to pin
#   for the stdio seam. Checked against PyPI on 2026-08-21: that name does
#   not exist, and neither do `dsh-sdk`, `deepseek-harness-client`, or
#   `deepseek-harness-runtime-bin`.
#
#   CAUTION, name collision. PyPI DOES carry `deepseek-harness` 0.2.0, and it
#   is NOT this project. Its Homepage is github.com/HenryZ838978/deepseek-
#   harness and its summary describes a protocol client for DeepSeek V4-Pro
#   and V4-Flash. Installing it under the belief that it is the deepseek-ai
#   harness SDK would pull an unrelated third-party package. Recorded here so
#   the mistake is made once, on paper, instead of in an install command.
#
#   The Python seam therefore has no pinnable artifact today. Its source is
#   `python/` inside the deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness repository. Until it
#   publishes, the stdio transport work has no supply-chain unit to review,
#   and the embedded web UI is the only integration that can be pinned.
